subject.title: feat(read): persist inbound media to workspace staging

question: Should non-sandbox inbound media receive a persistent workspace alias, and if so, which inbound-media lifecycle owner—not the read tool—owns its safe creation, retention, and per-run cleanup?
rationale: Current documentation establishes staging as an inbound/sandbox concern, while this PR adds a new persistent host-workspace behavior with security and lifecycle semantics that cannot be selected safely by mechanical repair alone.

options.title: Adopt lifecycle-owned staging
options.body: Approve a shared inbound-media staging owner with root-scoped writes, explicit per-run ownership, bounded retention, and focused proof for both sandboxed and non-sandboxed runs.

options.title: Keep staging sandbox-only
options.body: Retain the current sandbox staging behavior and close this host-workspace alias direction unless a separately designed product requirement establishes it.

options.title: Define a narrower workspace contract
options.body: Specify an explicit supported workspace alias contract first, then request a replacement PR built at that owner boundary.

recommendation.title: Adopt lifecycle-owned staging
recommendation.body: Approve a shared inbound-media staging owner with root-scoped writes, explicit per-run ownership, bounded retention, and focused proof for both sandboxed and non-sandboxed runs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent main history places inbound orchestration and its ownership boundary closest to this decision.
